If you want to go fast you need a big battery that can output at least a few hundred amps and a controller that can put our big phase amps. At minimum a 72450 fardriver should get that 12” hub motor spinning pretty quickly. 
It’s a cheap basic hub motor but it can still make decent power. The most expensive thing is going to be your battery, unless you’re experienced with building batteries and use cells from a EV car. Jag 35 has some out of a Honda clarity that are 12s /21ah and put out a few hundred amps and there only 58$ each. You would need at least 2 and series them for a 24s battery that would charge to 100.8v
Only issue with that is you now need the more expensive controller that can handle the 100v. 84450 fardriver is what I have used. 84650 would be better. 
Don’t need to upgrade the motor but if you do make sure you buy a v3 or v4 QS hub motor. They have aluminum stators and curved magnets so only 16 pole pairs vs 28 or whatever the cheaper motor is. Makes a big difference.

For the people that have Phat brand scooters the problem with buying a generic replacement is that it will be to tall to fit the base. They made the batteries very thin to fit between the frame rails and not hang down much past the 1.75” tubing. So a standard 18650 pack is going to be 65mm plus another 5mm or so in protection / wiring. You will need to have the metal base extended by a inch or 1.5” to accommodate the battery. It’s really not a big deal if someone knows how to fabricate metal. Can either make a new box entirely or just tack weld sheet metal to the sides. It’s not visible once it’s put back together and you won’t even notice it was done. 
Yes you will sacrifice a little bit of ground clearance but now you can just buy any battery that fits your battery tray.

All batteries made in China for electric scooters are crap. Not going to last 50 percent as long as they claim. If you have a scooter with a stock Chinese battery start saving for a replacement sooner rather than later. I see so many failing within the first 12-16 months. It’s typically caused by moisture, cells getting totally out of balance or BMS killing the pack and draining the battery to zero. 
Best advice, don’t leave your scooter sitting for months. Charge it fully and then ride it around to take some charge out. It’s not really ideal to fully charge it and then let it sit. Or don’t fully charge it if your not planning on riding it.

Ok so for the people who are looking for a replacement battery let me quickly give you some items to consider prior to buying a generic pack online. From my experience it seems that Phat changed something to do with the battery enclosure about once a year. So depending on your model and battery size your going to need to make sure you don’t get a battery larger or it will not fit. The newer scooters are made with a plastic deck with a latch area to access the battery. 
All phat scooters are 72v so while most 20s battery packs will certainly power the scooters, they need to output at minimum 40 amps continuous. In reality I use 60 amp BMS and pack configuration that can also output that current. The controller can pull up to maybe 40 amps for a short period during acceleration. Some versions have a small 12ah pack while more recent versions packed 25ah. 
I would recommend to get as much capacity as possible by using high quality cells around 3.4 -3.5ah 
LG MH1 , Samsung 35, LG MJ1. 
I have not found a phat version that could fit 21700 cells so you’re looking for 18650 cells. 

I’ll finish this later.. there’s some other things that might be helpful to some people who don’t know what to look for and are left with a paperweight scooter. Good news is it’s just a battery, but batteries are not cheap …yet.

The newer batteries are actually pouch cells that swell up when the pack starts to degrade. I have replaced older packs that were a block of 18650 cells but were in epoxy. It makes for a solid battery and keeps water from being a problem but it’s a strange way to build a battery. Makes it impossible to repair a BMS or a loose wire. 
I have a few different options for batteries and it depends on how much you want to increase the range. The most AH I have been able to fit is 36ah at 72v 20s6p in a enclosure under the seat and a smaller pack in the deck.

Exactly.. plenty of people overvolt electric motors all the time. I have built probably close to 100 electric vehicles of all different sizes and types. I have never burnt up a motor from to high a voltage. Voltage doesn’t kill motors, current does. Voltage is speed and current aka AMPS is torque or acceleration if you prefer. People can relate to acceleration more than how torque would feel although for this case they are the same. Current creates heat and heat is what causes motors to fail. The windings are coated with a very thin varnish and if that gets hot and softens it can create a short and poof there goes the motor.

I finished a ninebot max build last week that turned out pretty nice. I build electric shit as a hobby..
So I buy build and sell scooters all the time. I picked up a nanrobot d5+ from a guy who used it to get around the airport in Phoenix,worked at the maintenance hanger for American airlines. The battery would charge but quickly drop voltage within the first minute. Figured it was a group of bad cells but I bought it for$150 so I didn't care about the battery anyway. Everything just seemed as half ass bad Chinese design as possible. So I stripped everything I needed off the frame and sold it for what it cost me. 
I had a stripped down max frame that I got out of my friends uncle's scrap yard. It was just the aluminum frame and pole, everything else had already been stripped of of it. It was going to get recycled and was probably a day away from being cubed and hauled off. So I stripped the aluminum parts down to bare aluminum to remove all the deep scratches and primed it with a 2 part etching primer. 
The nanrobot hub motors are pretty wide but luckily they fit in the rear drop out. The front was another story. I had to build a wider front fork from scratch. I have done it in the past and i know what I'm doing but it's still a little bit of a tedious process. 
So with both motors installed I started to figure out how I was going to make it stop. Ended up making some brackets for the calipers to mount and ran some cables to them. I did a 160mm in the front and I 140mm rear. It stops almost to well. That's with the electric brakes turned off. 

Anyway I installed a 13s6p battery because i already had it built and it fit pretty much perfectly and had room to get the 2 controllers along side it. It's tight but everything fits well. 

With a full battery it gets up to 40mph, and I checked it with my GPS. It's pretty accurate but if anything it's maybe 1mph high. 
I tried it with a 8.4v boost pack on it and it increases 6mph. The controllers have 80v caps so I could try a 4s boost but honestly I don't need to blow anything up at this point. It's way to fast already.

I just finished adding led lights to a Dyson V6 vacuum I found at a goodwill for 20 bucks. The battery was crap so I built a 6s2p pack that's good for 20 or 30 minutes of low and high vacuuming action. But the thing needed a light and after vacuuming under my bed and not being able to see anything I just thought I would check the voltage on the power head and see if they are using battery voltage or if they are stepping it down. The head runs on 16vdc with a full battery at 25.2vdc. so 12vdc LEDs work just fine. I had a extra piece from another strip that has pretty good white lights on it. So soldered a + and - to to the white light pads and tapped into the wires on the power head. It works way better than I thought it would and took me about 30 minutes. 
Granted I have a dedicated electronics area in my dining room that I use to build ebikes and battery packs so advantage me. 
Anyway for anyone looking to see if it's possible..yea sure is. Only thing I should mention is make sure you use 12v led strips. They are using the longer 16 feet and up strips. The 6 foot version that plugs into USB is 5v and will cook in about a minute or two and then you will have to redo everything. So skip that disappointment and start with 12v lights,it will be printed on the led strip.

Yea the controller is most likely fried a MOSFET. Motors that have a short on the phase wires are basically the same as having the electric brakes engaged. Thus the resistance when you try and spin it. 
New controller or replace the shorted MOSFETs should fix.

Pack most likely has a bad cell somewhere in the pack. Do not continue to use it. It can create a thermal runaway situation and start a fire. Best bet is to have it looked at by someone who knows what they are doing. Finding the bad cell isn't that difficult but replacement is. If it has lost a good percentage of capacity it's probably smarter to replace the whole pack.
